dataflow.summary: Attacker-supplied local media -> user file selection -> full renderer read -> full browser decode and duration-dependent analysis, or unrestricted Python prediction/load -> unbounded result serialization -> buffered Rust IPC string -> JSON parsing and UI state.

attackPath.impact: Sustained CPU consumption, renderer or child-process memory exhaustion, UI freeze, app termination, and possible desktop-session memory pressure.

reachability.summary: Reachable through the production Import control when the user chooses the supplied file; Basic Pitch is selected when available and browser analysis is the fallback.

attackPath.severityRationale: Confirmed missing limits, but the attacker must deliver a file and persuade a local user to select it; the primary impact is recoverable local availability loss.

codeEvidence.explanation: The extension filter is a picker hint; no byte-size or media validation occurs before the complete file is materialized in renderer memory.
codeEvidence.label: Desktop import reads the selected file in full

codeEvidence.explanation: The complete compressed input and decoded buffer are retained, and total work grows with decoded duration.
codeEvidence.label: Browser analysis decodes and processes the complete duration

codeEvidence.explanation: Command::output has no deadline or cancellation path and buffers the child's full stdout and stderr.
codeEvidence.label: Native sidecar waits and buffers without limits

confidence.rationale: Direct source traces show whole-file reads and decoding, duration-dependent analysis, unbounded subprocess runtime/output, and no file-size, duration, event-count, timeout, cancellation, or single-flight control.

findings.remediation: Enforce documented compressed-size and decoded-duration limits before reading or spawning analysis; validate the actual media header; allow only one active analysis; add cancellation and an elapsed-time/sample budget; cap note events and IPC JSON size; replace unbounded Command::output with a killable child, wall-clock timeout, and bounded stdout/stderr handling; close AudioContext in a finally block.
remediationTests: Reject a file above the compressed-size limit before readFile or subprocess launch.
Reject or cancel audio above the decoded-duration or elapsed-time budget.
Verify a second import cannot begin while analysis is active.
Verify an overlong Basic Pitch process is killed and oversized stdout is rejected.
Verify AudioContext closes after both successful and failed decode.

rootCause.summary: The import boundary treats picker filtering as sufficient and applies no centralized resource policy before complete reads, decoder invocation, duration-proportional analysis, subprocess execution, or IPC JSON parsing.

severity.changeConditions: Raise severity if files can be opened automatically, arrive through a remote or shared ingestion channel, or the process runs with elevated privileges or on a shared service.
severity.rationale: The path requires a user to select attacker-supplied local media and primarily affects availability of the local app; impact can extend to desktop-session pressure, but exploitation is user assisted and recoverable by terminating the app.

findings.summary: A user-assisted oversized, extremely long, or event-dense audio file is read, decoded, analyzed, and serialized without byte, duration, runtime, output, event-count, or concurrency limits across both browser and Basic Pitch paths.
findings.title: Unbounded audio ingestion and analysis can exhaust CPU and memory

validation.counterevidence: The attack is local and user assisted, no shell is used, waveform output is capped at 520 points, and per-window Goertzel work is sampled. These reduce likelihood or some output but do not close the availability path.
validation.method: Static source trace and countercontrol review
validation.summary: Validated by tracing a selected file through pickAudio and analyzePicked into either WebAudio or the Python sidecar. File selection is explicit, shell injection is prevented by separate Command arguments, waveform output is capped, and the UI loop yields periodically; none of those controls bound file bytes, decoded duration, predicted events, child runtime/output, or overlapping imports.

dataflow.summary: User grants microphone and starts recording -> stream exists only in handleRecord closure -> user selects another workspace or MediaRecorder setup fails -> recording UI disappears or catch executes -> no application cleanup stops tracks.

attackPath.impact: Ambient audio may continue to be captured after the user reasonably expects the recording interaction to have ended, until another platform event or app termination releases the stream.

reachability.summary: Reachable through normal Record and workspace-switch controls in the unified production window; no separate renderer compromise is required.

attackPath.severityRationale: Normal UI navigation triggers the lifecycle gap and privacy impact is direct, while permission prompts and OS indicators limit covert capture.

codeEvidence.explanation: The MediaStream has no component-level owner or idempotent cleanup; setup failure after acquisition and view unmount bypass onstop.
codeEvidence.label: Tracks are stopped only after explicit recorder stop

codeEvidence.explanation: Selecting another workspace removes TranscribeWindow and its stop button while no cleanup effect stops the captured stream.
codeEvidence.label: Workspace changes unmount the recording view

confidence.rationale: The source stores only MediaRecorder in a ref, stops tracks solely in onstop, provides no unmount/error cleanup, and conditionally unmounts the transcription view when another workspace is selected.

findings.remediation: Store the MediaStream in a ref and implement one idempotent cleanup routine that stops every track, clears recorder handlers and timers, and resets refs/state. Invoke it on explicit stop, recorder error, setup failure, and component unmount. Add a maximum recording duration.
remediationTests: Start recording, switch to Library, and assert all microphone tracks have readyState ended.
Simulate MediaRecorder construction failure after getUserMedia and assert the acquired stream is stopped.
Trigger recorder error and verify cleanup runs exactly once.
Verify explicit Stop still creates and analyzes the intended recording.

rootCause.summary: Microphone ownership is tied to an event-handler closure rather than the component lifecycle, and cleanup is neither idempotent nor invoked from unmount, recorder error, or post-acquisition setup failure paths.

severity.changeConditions: Severity would be lower if the operating system or WebView guarantees immediate capture termination on component unmount; no such control is present in application source.
severity.rationale: Workspace switching is a normal, high-likelihood action and continued ambient microphone capture is a direct privacy impact, although platform permission and capture indicators reduce stealth.

findings.summary: The microphone MediaStream is stored only in a local closure and stopped only by MediaRecorder.onstop, so switching workspaces or failing after stream acquisition can leave capture active without a visible stop control.
findings.title: Microphone capture can continue after the recording view closes

validation.counterevidence: A user must grant microphone permission and start recording; explicit Stop correctly stops tracks, and the OS normally displays an active capture indicator.
validation.summary: Validated by tracing getUserMedia to the only track.stop call and confirming UnifiedApp conditionally unmounts TranscribeWindow. Explicit Stop reaches onstop, and OS permission/capture indicators exist, but unmount and setup-error paths do not.

dataflow.summary: Repeated local imports or recordings -> new Blob URL per item -> store replacement drops the old string without revokeObjectURL; decode-failing files -> new AudioContext -> exception before close.

attackPath.impact: Memory and audio resources accumulate for the page lifetime, amplifying sluggishness and eventually causing renderer degradation or termination.

reachability.summary: Reachable through repeated use of the production Import or Record controls, especially with large or invalid media.

attackPath.severityRationale: The leak is deterministic but generally requires repeated actions and affects recoverable local availability.

codeEvidence.code: importSong: (song, audioUrl) => set((state) => ({ songs: [song, ...state.songs.filter((item) => item.id !== song.id)], activeSong: song, audioUrl, currentTime: 0, duration: song.duration, isPlaying: false })),
codeEvidence.explanation: The old Blob URL is discarded from state but remains registered and retains its Blob until explicitly revoked or the page ends.
codeEvidence.label: Store replaces audio URL without revoking the previous URL

codeEvidence.explanation: Any decode or analysis exception skips close because no try/finally owns the context.
codeEvidence.label: AudioContext closes only on successful completion

confidence.rationale: All object URL creation and revocation sites were traced: export URLs are revoked, but audio import/recording URLs are overwritten without revocation, and AudioContext.close is outside a finally block.

findings.remediation: Revoke the previous owned playback Blob URL when replacing it and revoke the current URL on final application teardown after pausing playback. Wrap every AudioContext in try/finally and close it on success and failure.
remediationTests: Import two files and assert revokeObjectURL is called for the first URL exactly once.
Make decodeAudioData reject and assert AudioContext.close is still awaited.
Verify export URL cleanup remains intact and current playback remains usable until replacement.

rootCause.summary: Renderer audio resources lack explicit ownership rules across replacement, failure, and teardown; cleanup is implemented for temporary export URLs but not imported playback URLs or exceptional AudioContext paths.

severity.changeConditions: Raise severity if imports become automatic, attacker-triggerable without user interaction, or the application is expected to run unattended for long periods.
severity.rationale: The issue requires repeated local actions or large failing files and primarily degrades the current app process, but the source establishes persistent per-page resource retention.

findings.summary: Import and recording Blob URLs are never revoked when replaced, while AudioContext.close runs only on successful browser analysis, allowing repeated imports or decode failures to retain renderer memory and audio resources.
findings.title: Repeated imports leak Blob URLs and failed AudioContexts

validation.counterevidence: Only one URL remains referenced in Zustand, successful analysis closes its context, and app/page termination eventually releases page-owned resources.
validation.summary: Validated by enumerating createObjectURL and revokeObjectURL calls and following AudioContext.close. Only the export URL is revoked; imported and recorded audio URLs are not. The analysis context closes only after all awaited work succeeds.
